chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Among what Musa (peace be upon him) whispered to Allah was: 'O Lord, what is for the one who washes the dead?' So He said: 'I wash him from his sins just as his mother gave birth to him.'

key_terms.غَسَّلَ: to wash (specifically the ritual washing of the dead)
key_terms.نَاجَى: to whisper or converse privately with God

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for washing a deceased believer's body according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the profound spiritual merit of ghasl (ritual washing) by framing it as a divine act of purification that mirrors the soul's pristine state at birth. In Shia scholarship, this narrative underscores the continuity between physical care for the deceased and the forgiveness of the living, emphasizing that the act serves as a means of cleansing one's own sins through the service rendered to the believer. The metaphor of returning to the state of 'innocence' (aslamahu) reflects the concept of fitrah, linking the ritual to the restoration of spiritual purity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Mhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Among what Musa<sup>as</sup> whispered to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with, was: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is for the one who washes the dead?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “I<sup>azwj</sup> would Wash him from his sins to just as he was when his mother gave birth to him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sinan from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One of the matters that Moses spoke about before Allah was this, “O Allah, what is the reward for one who washes a dead body?” The answer was, “I wash his sins as if his mother has just given him birth.’””
